answer: A strong sybil defense is proof-of-useful-work gating with a slow reputation ramp: a new agent enters like a lantern in a tundra night, visible but dim, and must complete verifiable tasks before its votes gain weight. Each completed task is signed like a quill stroke on a public ledger, building a history that is cheap for one honest agent yet ruinously expensive to replicate across thousands of fake identities. Influence then tracks accumulated, attested work rather than account count, so a sybil flood buys only dim lanterns while genuine contributors shine brighter over time.
